plans.name: What you do now

tabs.why: This is what you grow now. We compare every other choice with it.
tabs.evidence: We replayed the weather from 2002 to 2025. Harvest was 72 out of 100 on average. Without our rain fix, it was 73. Very dry years: 7 of 24. Harvest numbers are computer estimates. GPM IMERG: seen from space, 0.1 deg (about 10 km), 2001-2025. NASA POWER: worked out by computer, 0.5 x 0.625 deg (about 55 km), 2001-2025. GRACE and GRACE-FO: seen from space, about 300 km, 2002-2026. ISRIC SoilGrids: worked out by computer, 250 m, one map.
tabs.benefits: You already know how to grow these. Changing crops can keep pests and diseases down.
tabs.unknown: This is a sample field, not yours. Nearby parts share one soil map. Planting dates are typical ones, not yours. We guessed how thirst hurts rice. If you can water, rice stands in water. Without water, rice lives on rain alone. Your water is unknown, so we show both. NASA checks its rain against ground rain gauges. Near here, those gauge reports stopped in 2017. Then NASA's rain here jumped too high. We lowered rain from 2017 to match before. That may also hide a real change. Stored water is measured for a wide area. It is not your own well. We may count too many freezing nights. Prices and markets are not included.
tabs.check: Ask your local farm advisor first. Check how much water you really have. Try it on one small part first. You know your land best.

tips: Rice gets most thirsty in October. Water it then if you can.
Potato gets most thirsty in January. Water it then if you can.
Cover bare soil with straw in March.

tabs_ne.why: यो तपाईंले अहिले लगाउने बाली हो। हामी अरू हरेक विकल्पलाई यसैसँग दाँज्छौं।
tabs_ne.evidence: २००२ देखि २०२५ सम्मको मौसम फेरि चलायौं। औसत उब्जनी १०० मा ७२ थियो। हाम्रो वर्षा सुधारबिना यो ७३ थियो। खडेरी परेका वर्ष: २४ मध्ये ७। उब्जनीका अङ्क कम्प्युटरका अनुमान हुन्। GPM IMERG: अन्तरिक्षबाट देखिएको, ०.१ deg (about १० km), २००१-२०२५। NASA POWER: कम्प्युटरले निकालेको, ०.५ x ०.६२५ deg (about ५५ km), २००१-२०२५। GRACE and GRACE-FO: अन्तरिक्षबाट देखिएको, about ३०० km, २००२-२०२६। ISRIC SoilGrids: कम्प्युटरले निकालेको, २५० m, one map।
tabs_ne.benefits: यी बाली लगाउन तपाईंलाई पहिले नै आउँछ। बाली फेर्दा कीरा र रोग घट्न सक्छ।
tabs_ne.unknown: यो नमुना खेत हो, तपाईंको होइन। नजिकका भागहरूको माटोको नक्सा एउटै छ। रोप्ने मिति सामान्य हुन्, तपाईंका होइनन्। धानमा तिर्खाको असर हाम्रो अनुमान हो। पानी दिन सक्नुहुन्छ भने धान पानीमा रहन्छ। पानी नभए धान वर्षामा मात्र भर पर्छ। पानीको स्रोत थाहा नभएकाले दुवै देखाएका छौं। नासाले आफ्नो वर्षाको नाप जमिनका वर्षा मापकसँग मिलाउँछ। यहाँ नजिक ती मापकका खबर २०१७ मा रोकिए। त्यसपछि यहाँ नासाको वर्षा धेरै बढी देखियो। हामीले २०१७ देखिको वर्षा पहिलेजस्तै हुने गरी घटायौं। यसले साँच्चै भएको फेरबदल पनि लुकाउन सक्छ। जम्मा पानी ठूलो क्षेत्रको नापिएको हो। यो तपाईंको आफ्नै इनार होइन। हामीले तुषारो परेका रात बढी गनेका हुन सक्छौं। बजार र मूल्य यसमा समावेश छैनन्।
tabs_ne.check: पहिले नजिकको कृषि प्राविधिकलाई सोध्नुहोस्। तपाईंसँग साँच्चै कति पानी छ, जाँच्नुहोस्। पहिले एउटा सानो भागमा मात्र गरेर हेर्नुहोस्। आफ्नो जमिन तपाईंलाई नै राम्रो थाहा छ।

tips_ne: धानलाई कात्तिक (अक्टोबर–नोभेम्बर)मा सबैभन्दा धेरै तिर्खा लाग्छ। सक्नुहुन्छ भने त्यतिबेला पानी दिनुहोस्।
आलुलाई माघ (जनवरी–फेब्रुअरी)मा सबैभन्दा धेरै तिर्खा लाग्छ। सक्नुहुन्छ भने त्यतिबेला पानी दिनुहोस्।

plans.name: Fill the empty months

tabs.evidence: We replayed the weather from 2002 to 2025. Harvest was 90 out of 100 on average. Very dry years: 6 of 24. Harvest numbers are computer estimates. GPM IMERG: seen from space, 0.1 deg (about 10 km), 2001-2025. NASA POWER: worked out by computer, 0.5 x 0.625 deg (about 55 km), 2001-2025. GRACE and GRACE-FO: seen from space, about 300 km, 2002-2026. ISRIC SoilGrids: worked out by computer, 250 m, one map.
tabs.benefits: Harvest: about 18 more, out of 100. Needs less water than now. Ground stays covered more of the year. Wheat roots reach water deeper down.
tabs.unknown: This is a sample field, not yours. Nearby parts share one soil map. Planting dates are typical ones, not yours. We guessed how thirst hurts rice. If you can water, rice stands in water. Without water, rice lives on rain alone. Your water is unknown, so we show both. NASA checks its rain against ground rain gauges. Near here, those gauge reports stopped in 2017. Then NASA's rain here jumped too high. We lowered rain from 2017 to match before. That may also hide a real change. Stored water is measured for a wide area. It is not your own well. We may count too many freezing nights. Prices and markets are not included.
tabs.check: Ask your local farm advisor first. Ask if wheat seed is sold nearby. Ask neighbours when they plant wheat. Lentil after rice is another choice. It feeds the soil. Changing crop kinds keeps pests down. Check how much water you really have. Wheat here usually needs watering. Check you can water it. Try it on one small part first. You know your land best.

tips: Rice gets most thirsty in June. Water it then if you can.
Wheat gets most thirsty in February. Water it then if you can.
Cover bare soil with straw in April.

words.en: NASA's rain maps are checked against rain gauges. Around this field, gauge reports stopped in 2017. Before, the gauges set almost all of it. After, the picture from space took over. Its yearly rain here jumped to 2730 mm. Before, it was 1840 mm. The nearest town's usual rain: 1380 mm. We scaled each month from 2017 back down. Each month now matches its earlier years. We tested this on years we kept aside. Monthly error at the airport: 94 mm before. After our fix: 31 mm. This fix may also hide real change. So we show both, as a range.
words.ne: नासाको वर्षाको नक्सा वर्षा मापकसँग जाँचिन्छ। यो खेत वरिपरि मापकका खबर २०१७ मा रोकिए। पहिले, धेरैजसो नाप मापकले नै मिलाउँथे। त्यसपछि, अन्तरिक्षबाट हेरेको नापले ठाउँ लियो। यहाँको वार्षिक वर्षा २७३० मिलिमिटर पुग्यो। पहिले यो १८४० मिलिमिटर थियो। नजिकको सहरको सामान्य वर्षा: १३८० मिलिमिटर। हामीले २०१७ देखि हरेक महिना घटायौं। अब हरेक महिना पहिलेका वर्षसँग मिल्छ। यो जाँच अलग राखेका वर्षमा गर्‍यौं। विमानस्थलमा मासिक फरक: पहिले ९४ मिलिमिटर। सुधारपछि: ३१ मिलिमिटर। यस सुधारले साँचो फेरबदल पनि लुकाउन सक्छ। त्यसैले हामी दुवै देखाउँछौं, दायराका रूपमा।

choices.choice: Claude's proposal, owner-approved 2026-11-12 (owner's batch decisions, item 1) (REVIEW_NOTES M2): the weather table fails loudly if POWER fills more than 5% of any year's days (about 18 days), so a partly failed GPM download cannot turn into POWER rain unnoticed. Every filled day stays flagged (rain_filled, rain_source)
Owner-approved 2026-11-12 (proposed by Claude: the 330-record rule leaves no Tmin years at Kathmandu Airport; 200 keeps 2015, 2016, 2017, 2019, 2021, 2022, 2023)

Claude's choice, owner-approved 2026-11-12 (step-4 review item 5): map at the 1st to 99th percentiles. Beyond the ends keep the end-quantile difference: Gudmundsson et al. 2012 state this for values above the training range; applying it below as well is Claude's choice

Owner, 2026-11-12: let the three sources vote; if GPM agrees with the station, mark the day a real local storm. The 'suspect station' half is Claude's reading, owner-approved 2026-11-12 (step-4 review item 5). Caveat (REVIEW_NOTES H2, 2026-11-12): every Kathmandu Airport record is GHCN S-flag 'S', derived from synoptic reports, which the GHCN readme says to use with caution, especially for rain; a 'station value suspect' or 'real local storm' label rests on that series

Straight row and 'good' condition are Claude's choices for a flat valley-floor field, owner-approved 2026-11-12 (step-4 review item 5). Kept for the placeholder field, a 1.6 deg (about 2.8%) valley floor where a 30 m elevation model shows no terraces (owner-approved 2026-11-12 (owner's batch decisions, item 20)); revisit for a terraced hill field, which needs the contoured or contoured-and-terraced rows

choices.choice: Claude's choice, owner-approved 2026-11-12 (step-4 review item 5); start, middle or end in step 7 owner-approved 2026-11-12 (owner's batch decisions, item 10). Windows from the FAO Crop Calendar, Nepal Hill zone (crops.json calendar sources)

Step 7's plan generator may also sow at the window's start or end and keeps the sequences that fit without overlap; the current plan stays at the middle. No relay cropping, so maize then rice stays out (rice's latest default sowing is 15 Jul)

choices.choice: Claude's choice, owner-approved 2026-11-12 (owner's batch decisions, item 13): a winter crop sown in Oct-Nov belongs to the year of its harvest (potato sown 30 Oct 2001 counts in 2002)

choices.choice: Claude's choice, owner-approved 2026-11-12 (owner's batch decisions, item 14): the contract (replay_year) has one harvest and one dry-day count per year
choices.value: a year's harvest is the mean of its crops' harvest percentages; its dry days are their sum

choices.choice: Claude's choice, owner-approved 2026-11-12 (owner's batch decisions, item 2), for the TEMPORARY station-rain dry run only (never exported): a year is used only if the station has rain on at least 90% of its days; missing days are filled from POWER and flagged

Rainfall deciles (Gibbs & Maher 1967, Bureau of Meteorology Bulletin No. 48; cited by WMO & GWP 2016, Handbook of Drought Indicators and Indices, WMO-No. 1173, pp. 11-12). Classes from Hayes, 'Drought Indices', National Drought Mitigation Center (archived 2009-05-10, https://webarchive.library.unt.edu/eot2008/20090510055327id_/http://www.drought.unl.edu/whatis/indices.htm): 'deciles 1-2: lowest 20% much below normal'. Applied to each crop's season rain over the replay record, decile = ceil(10 x rank / n) with average ranks for ties. The method wants a long record (Australia uses 100 years); 25 seasons is short. Calling 'much below normal' a drought: Claude's choice, owner-approved 2026-11-12 (owner's batch decisions, item 17)

Claude's choice, owner-approved 2026-11-12 (owner's batch decisions, item 19): the contract allows one event per year; drought before flood, in the contract's enum order. Frost is no longer a replay event (owner, 2026-11-12, REVIEW_NOTES M1): the frost Tmin is known to overcount cold nights, so frost is shown only as a risk band in the monthly calendar (diary.months[].frost), never per year. The removed per-year rule (wheat 0 C mid-season, potato -2 C whole season, with its sources) is kept in METHOD_NOTES.md for the record
choices.value: ['drought', 'flood']

choices.choice: Seasonal Mann-Kendall test (Hirsch, Slack & Smith 1982; Hirsch & Slack 1984; pymannkendall.seasonal_test) at the conventional 5% level. Claude's choice of test, owner-approved 2026-11-13: the test fits a monthly series with a strong yearly cycle and gaps (GRACE/GRACE-FO 2017-2018)
Claude's choice, owner-approved 2026-11-13 (D7: 'the rule for steady and for confidence is set and cited in rules.yaml at step 6'): 'steady' = no trend at the test's 5% level
choices.value: steady unless p < alpha; then falling or rising by the sign of the seasonal Sen slope

choices.choice: Claude's choice, owner-approved 2026-11-13, no published source: how strongly the record shows a change (1 - the test's p-value); not a probability that the direction is right

Claude's proposal, owner-approved 2026-11-12 (owner's batch decisions, item 24): five readings of one cup 'barely differ' (VALIDATION 5.2) when max - min is at most 3 points on the probe's 0-100% moisture scale; the variance of the same five readings is recorded as the probe's error variance R (CLAUDE.md 'Probe fusion'). No standard was opened; the robot teammate may tighten it after the first bench test

Owner, 2026-11-13 (decision 1) is about this field: 'the rain gauges behind NASA's correction disappeared around this field in January 2017'. Claude's reading: a field abroad (build step 11) is corrected only after its own rain check B finds the same break, since gauge networks differ by country
choices.value: ['demo']

choices.choice: Claude's reading, fixed 2026-11-13 before the Late check (IMERG Late 2014-2019) was read: only IMERG Final days are scaled, and only they set the factors. The 92 IMERG Late days (Oct-Dec 2025, D1) are left as they are, because Late uses a climatological gauge calibration, not the monthly gauges that vanished, so the 2017 loss cannot reach it; the Late check tests that. POWER-filled days (none on the demo field) are another source and are not scaled either. If the Late check shows Late stepping up in 2017 as Final does, this is put back to the owner. Late check (2026-11-13, VALIDATION 3.9b): Late does not step with Final (1.13 against 1.62), but it is wetter than gauge-adjusted Final in 2014-2016 (Final/Late 0.64-0.85) and about equal to Final from 2017 (1.00-1.13): Late sits at the un-gauged level, so whether to scale the 92 Late days too is put to the owner
choices.value: ['final']

choices.choice: Owner-approved 2026-11-13 (batch: every threshold with a published source). Claude's choice: stop the search at 30 September, so a year with no qualifying start has no onset (reported as none, never guessed). DHM Climate Division, 'Monsoon Onset and Withdrawal date information' (1968-2024), p. 1, dhm.gov.np: normal onset (eastern Nepal) 13 June, latest on record 27 June 1982; normal withdrawal 2 October

Owner-approved 2026-11-13 (batch: every threshold with a published source). Claude's reading of CLAUDE.md: a wet day has at least 1 mm, the complement of the rule's own dry day 'under 1 mm per day'; ETCCDI list of 27 indices (etccdi.pacificclimate.org): 'wet days, w (RR >= 1mm)'

CLAUDE.md (owner): 'the first run of at least 2 wet days'. Owner-approved 2026-11-13 (batch: every threshold with a published source). Claude's reading: the onset day d is itself wet, and the wet days need not be consecutive, as in Moron, Robertson & Boer 2009 (J. Climate, sec. 2c): 'the first wet day of the first 5-day sequence receiving at least 40 mm'

Claude's choice, owner-approved 2026-11-13 (CLAUDE.md: 'require a minimum clear-pixel fraction per image'): an HLS image counts for the field only when at least 75% of the field's pixels are clear (Fmask bits 0-5 zero) and hold NDVI; for the 60 m demo field (4 HLS pixels) that is 3 of 4. No published source found: the HLS v2.0 User Guide (Apr 2026, sec. 6.4) gives the Fmask bits but no clear fraction; the one parcel rule found masks parcels with more than 50% of pixels masked (Sitokonstantinou 2022, arXiv 2211.12584, App. A.1), so 75% is stricter

Owner-approved 2026-11-13 (batch: every threshold with a published source). Claude's choice: MOD13Q1 pixel reliability 0 ('good data') only; 1 (marginal), 2 (snow/ice) and 3 (cloudy) are dropped. Rank keys from the file's own Legend attribute; MOD13 User's Guide C6.1 (V3.10), Table 4: 0 'Good Data, Use with confidence', 1 'Marginal data, Useful, but look at other QA information'

Claude's choice, owner-approved 2026-11-13: an HLS observation and a MODIS composite are compared when their dates are at most 8 days apart (half of MODIS's 16-day composite; no source for the limit). The MODIS date is the pixel's own 'composite day of the year' (MOD13 User's Guide sec. 5.1: 'adjacent selected pixels may originate from different days')

Claude's choice, owner-approved 2026-11-13: Savitzky-Golay window on the daily interpolated series (no source for 31 days: Chen et al. 2004 smoothed 10-day composites, not opened past the abstract; TIMESAT 3.3 manual, row 34, gives a rough half-window of a quarter of the points per year, far wider, and warns a large window 'affects the possibility to follow a rapid change')

Owner-approved 2026-11-13 (batch: every threshold with a published source). Claude's choice within the published range: season start and end at 20% of the rise and of the fall (TIMESAT 3.3 manual sec. 4.4: start at 'a user defined level (often a certain fraction of the seasonal amplitude) measured from the left minimum level', end from the right minimum; its examples use 0.5 and 0.3; NASA MCD12Q2 uses 15%, 50% and 90% of the green-up amplitude)

Owner-approved 2026-11-13 (batch: every threshold with a published source). PELT (Killick, Fearnhead & Eckley 2012) penalty; the 2 parameters per kink is Claude's reading, owner-approved 2026-11-13: sigma^2 x 2 x ln(n), a BIC-type penalty with 2 parameters per kink (its place and the change of slope); sigma = scatter of the clear observations about the smoothed curve (Killick, Fearnhead & Eckley 2012, arXiv:1101.1438 sec. 2: 'SIC, also known as BIC ... (beta = p log n), where p is the number of additional parameters introduced by adding a changepoint', for a cost of twice the negative log-likelihood, i.e. sigma^2 p ln n for a sum of squares; p = 2 is Claude's reading)
Claude's choice, owner-approved 2026-11-13: no segment shorter than 5 days

Claude's choices, owner-approved 2026-11-13: random forest (scikit-learn) with 300 trees, leaves of at least 5 days, fixed seed; slopes over 15 days; 'time since green-up' = days since the lowest smoothed NDVI of the last 120 days; rain and temperature over the last 30 days; labels smoothed by a 15-day majority; growing runs shorter than 30 days are not seasons
